html:
The Zanzibar Revolution of 12 January 1964 overthrew the sultan of Zanzibar, a month after independence from Britain, and ended Arab rule of the islands.

Zanzibar had become independent under a government dominated by the Arab minority. African revolutionaries led by John Okello stormed police stations and took power. Thousands of Arabs and South Asians were killed and many fled. Abeid Karume of the Afro-Shirazi Party became president.

On 26 April 1964, Karume and Julius Nyerere joined Zanzibar with Tanganyika in a union, named Tanzania later that year. Zanzibar kept its own president and government. It ended the sultanate founded by Said bin Sultan in Zanzibar, whose wealth rested on cloves and slavery.
sum: The Zanzibar Revolution of 12 January 1964 overthrew the sultan of Zanzibar, a month after independence from Britain, and ended Arab rule of the islands.
